newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil delays civil service reform bill vote 2 wks.
newsitem.headline: Brazil delays civil service reform bill vote 2 wks.

text.p: A first vote in Brazil's Chamber of Deputies on a bill to reform the civil service will only take place in two weeks' time and not on Wednesday as previously scheduled, a deputy in charge of the bill said.

After meeting with President Fernando Henrique Cardoso, Deputy Wellington Moreira Franco said the government had been unable to overcome resistance to a proposed pay cap included in the reform which would hit many lawmakers' incomes.
Moreira Franco said Cardoso had given full support to his bill during their meeting and had insisted that the pay cap be maintained.
"We will not give in," the lawmaker told reporters as he left the presidential palace.
The civil service reform is a constitutional amendment and requires two three-fifths majorities in each house of Congress.
It is considered one the government's most important tools in reducing public sector spending, but has been languishing in Congress since August 1995.
One key clause would allow states and municipalities spending more than 60 percent of receipts on payrolls to dismiss workers who currently enjoy job guarantees.
The pay cap is another central point, limiting public sector workers and pensioners to a maximum of 10,800 reais ($10,285) a month in total pay and benefits.
Newspapers have said 140 of the lower house's 513 members stand to lose out from that clause -- although whips say the number is lower -- making approval of the reform difficult.
Opponents in Congress of the ceiling have suggested the inclusion of a higher limit for doctors, lawyers and other qualified professionals, including deputies and senators.
